root_causes: Inefficient initial planning: the planner issued long-horizon Rearrange actions for cup_0 and squeezer_1 from far away instead of first navigating agents closer, causing many low-reward intermediate steps.

Redundant repeated actions: the same Rearrange[cup_0, on, bench_51] and Rearrange[squeezer_1, on, bench_51] commands were reissued across multiple steps (16–19, 22–24) even though progress was already underway.
Poor coordination between agents: one agent frequently executed Wait[None] (e.g., steps 22–26, 27–29) while the other was active, underutilizing available parallelism in a two-agent setting.

Delayed object acquisition: toy_food_2 was left on table_30 until very late (steps 27–30), resulting in extra navigation and planning cycles instead of batching the three objects’ transfers efficiently.

Over-reliance on replanning around the same subgoals: multiple replan_pre_window and replan_post_window cycles occurred around the same rearrangement actions, increasing step count and reducing reward without improving outcome.
improvement_suggestions: Introduce a navigation-then-manipulation macro-strategy so that agents first move close to target objects and the bench before issuing Rearrange, reducing long-distance rearrange calls.
Limit repeated dispatch of identical Rearrange commands by tracking in-progress object transfers and avoiding re-issuing the same subgoal unless it clearly failed.
Exploit two-agent parallelism: while one agent transports an object, assign the other to fetch the next object or to pre-position near the bench rather than waiting.

Batch planning for all three objects so that mug, squeezer, and toy food are scheduled in an order that minimizes back-and-forth navigation, ideally with one agent focusing on source collection and the other on bench placement.
Tune replanning triggers to reduce unnecessary replan_pre_window and replan_post_window cycles when progress is being made, favoring continuation of successful actions over immediate replans.
overall_assessment: The task was completed successfully with all three objects placed on the bench, but the trajectory contained significant inefficiencies from repeated rearrange calls, underused parallelism, and excessive replanning.
task_instruction: Put the mug, squeezer, and toy food on the bench in the entryway.
